allow_squash_merge.title: Allow Squash Merge

squash_merge_commit_title.description: Default title for squash merge commits: 'PR_TITLE' or 'COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE'.
squash_merge_commit_title.human_parameter_description: Choose the default title for squash-merge commits—use the PR title or the original commit/PR title.

base.description: The name of the branch you want the changes pulled into. This must be an existing branch on the current (target) repository. You cannot submit a pull request to one repository that requests a merge to a base branch of another repository.

examples: This PR introduces a new feature that does X, Y, and Z.

For cross-repository pull requests, namespace `head` with the source owner and branch, like `username:branch`.
head.human_parameter_description: The source branch that contains your changes. CRITICAL: This branch must already exist in the repository before you can create a pull request. The typical workflow is: 1) Create a new branch, 2) Push commits to that branch, 3) Then create a PR. If the branch is in a fork or another repository, use the format owner:branch.

line.title: Line
line.description: **[LINE-BASED MODE]** Line number in the diff for the comment. Required when using line-based mode (must be used with `side`). For multi-line comments, this is the last line of the range. Do not use with position or in_reply_to parameters.

side.title: SideEnm
side.description: **[LINE-BASED MODE]** Side of the diff (`LEFT` or `RIGHT`) for the comment. Required when using line-based mode with the `line` parameter. For multi-line comments, refers to the last line of the range. Do not use with position or in_reply_to parameters. **IMPORTANT:** Use `LEFT` only for deletions that appear in red in the diff. Use `RIGHT` for additions (green) or unchanged context lines (white). Attempting to comment on LEFT side lines that are not visible deletions in the diff will result in a 'could not be resolved' error.

name: Create a dependency snapshot

input_parameters.title: CreateASnapshotOfDependenciesForARepositoryRequest

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: Git reference (fully qualified, e.g., `refs/heads/main`) of the repository branch/tag that triggered this snapshot.
ref.human_parameter_description: The branch or tag ref that triggered the snapshot, like refs/heads/main or refs/tags/v1.0. This ties the snapshot to a specific ref.

sha.title: Sha
sha.description: Commit SHA (maximum 40 characters) associated with this dependency snapshot.
sha.human_parameter_description: The commit SHA for the code state you’re capturing. Use the full 40‑character SHA to avoid ambiguity.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Repository name, without `.git` extension (name is not case-sensitive).
repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository (without .git) that you want to snapshot. This identifies which project’s dependencies to capture.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Account owner of the repository (name is not case-sensitive).
owner.human_parameter_description: The user or organization that owns the repository you want to snapshot. This tells us where to find the repo.

job__id.title: Job  Id
job__id.description: Optional external ID of the job that generated this snapshot.
job__id.human_parameter_description: An ID for the CI job or process that produced this snapshot. It helps you trace the snapshot back to the run that created it.

scanned.title: Scanned
scanned.description: UTC timestamp (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the snapshot was taken.
scanned.human_parameter_description: The exact time the snapshot was taken, in UTC ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2023-10-26T14:30:00Z). This timestamps when the dependency state was captured.

version.title: Version
version.description: Version of the dependency snapshot submission, typically of the manifest or lock file format.
version.human_parameter_description: The version number of the snapshot format you’re submitting. Use the version that matches your manifest/lockfile format or tool.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Optional user-defined metadata as a JSON string for domain-specific information. Limited to 8 keys with scalar values (e.g., string, number, boolean). Example: '{"key1": "value1", "key2": 123}'
metadata.human_parameter_description: Optional key‑value details you want to attach to this snapshot (up to 8 simple values) as a JSON string. Use this for filtering, auditing, or custom notes.

manifests.title: Manifests
manifests.description: Optional collection of package manifests as a JSON string (e.g., package-lock.json, pom.xml). Keys are manifest file names; values detail dependencies. Example: '{"package-lock.json": {"name": "...", "resolved": {...}}}'
manifests.human_parameter_description: A mapping of manifest file names to their dependency details from your scan as a JSON string (e.g., package-lock.json, pom.xml). Include the files you analyzed.

detector__url.title: Detector  Url
detector__url.description: Optional URL of the detector tool used.
detector__url.human_parameter_description: A URL for the dependency scanning tool or its documentation. Helpful for reference.

detector__name.title: Detector  Name
detector__name.description: Optional name of the tool used to detect dependencies.
detector__name.human_parameter_description: The name of the tool that scanned your project for dependencies. Examples include 'dependency-check' or similar tools.

job__html__url.title: Job  Html  Url
job__html__url.description: Optional URL for the job that generated this snapshot.
job__html__url.human_parameter_description: A link to the CI job or build page that created this snapshot. Useful for others to see logs and details.

job__correlator.title: Job  Correlator
job__correlator.description: Optional string to group snapshots. For a given `job.correlator` and `detector.name`, only the 'latest' snapshot is current. Useful to distinguish detection runs (e.g., concatenating GITHUB_WORKFLOW and GITHUB_JOB).
job__correlator.human_parameter_description: A string that groups related snapshots from the same workflow or run. It helps keep only the latest snapshot current for that group.

detector__version.title: Detector  Version
detector__version.description: Optional version of the detector tool used.

input_parameters.title: FindPullRequestsRequest

page.title: Page
page.description: Page number of results to fetch.
page.human_parameter_description: Which page of results to view. Use this to move through large result sets.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: Filter by specific repository. Can be provided in 'owner/repo' format (e.g., 'facebook/react'), or as just the repo name when used with the owner parameter. When owner and repo are both provided and have the same value, they are combined as 'owner/repo'. When omitted along with owner, search scope is determined by for_authenticated_user flag. The repository must exist and be accessible with your token. Prefer 'owner/repo' format; bare repo name without the `owner` parameter causes invalid repository format errors.
repo.human_parameter_description: Limit the search to a single repository. You can provide it in 'owner/repo' format like 'facebook/react', or just the repository name (like 'react') when also providing the owner parameter separately. If you want to search repository 'notetake/notetake', you can use repo='notetake/notetake' OR owner='notetake' with repo='notetake'. Leave blank to search across multiple repositories. The repository must exist and be accessible with your token.

sort.title: Sort
sort.description: Field to sort results by. Set explicitly to 'updated' with `order=desc` when recency matters; default behavior may return best-match relevance ordering instead.
sort.human_parameter_description: Choose how to sort the results, such as by last updated, creation date, or number of comments.

label.title: Label
label.description: Filter by label name.
label.human_parameter_description: Only include PRs with a particular label, such as 'bug' or 'enhancement'.

order.title: Order
order.human_parameter_description: Pick ascending or descending order for the selected sort field. Most recent first is 'desc'.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Filter by repository owner (user or organization). Can be used alone to search all repositories for an owner, or combined with repo parameter to specify owner and repo separately. When both owner and repo are provided, the search is scoped to 'owner/repo'. When omitted along with repo, search scope is determined by for_authenticated_user flag. The owner must exist and repositories must be accessible with your token.
owner.human_parameter_description: Search within all repositories for a specific user or organization (like 'microsoft'), or provide it together with the repo parameter to specify owner and repository separately. If owner='notetake' and repo='notetake', the search will be in repository 'notetake/notetake'. Leave blank to search across multiple owners. The owner must exist and repositories must be accessible with your token.

query.title: Query
query.description: Optional search query for PR title, description, or commit messages. Supports GitHub search syntax including label filters (e.g., 'label:bug'), logical operators (AND, OR, NOT), and text search. If not provided, PRs will be listed based on other filter parameters. Type qualifiers (type:pr, is:pr, is:issue, type:issue) are automatically normalized. When using logical operators with qualifiers like labels, the query is automatically grouped for proper parsing. When omitting query, ensure at least one structured filter parameter is provided; passing no query and no filters may cause validation errors. Prefer dedicated parameters (`label`, `state`, `author`) over embedding qualifiers in the query string. Exact title matching is not supported; post-filter on title client-side if needed.
query.human_parameter_description: Enter words or phrases that appear in the PR title, description, or commit messages. You can also use GitHub search qualifiers like 'label:bug' or combine them with logical operators like 'label:bug OR label:enhancement'. This is optional - you can filter PRs by repository, state, owner, and other parameters without a text search query. Do not include type qualifiers like 'type:pr' or 'is:pr' as they are handled automatically.

state.title: State
state.description: Filter by PR state: 'open', 'closed', or 'all'.
state.human_parameter_description: Choose which PR states to include: open, closed, or all. Use 'all' to see every state.

author.title: Author
author.description: Filter by PR author username. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.
author.human_parameter_description: Find PRs created by a particular GitHub user. Enter their exact username (case-insensitive). GitHub usernames can only contain letters, numbers, and hyphens (no dots or other special characters). The user must exist on GitHub.

assignee.title: Assignee
assignee.description: Filter by PR assignee username. Use '@me' for current user. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.
assignee.human_parameter_description: Find PRs assigned to a specific user. Enter their exact username or use '@me' for yourself. GitHub usernames can only contain letters, numbers, and hyphens (no dots or other special characters). The user must exist on GitHub.

language.title: Language
language.description: Filter by programming language.
language.human_parameter_description: Restrict results to PRs in repositories primarily using a specific language, like Python or JavaScript.

mentions.title: Mentions
mentions.description: Filter by username mentioned in PR. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.
mentions.human_parameter_description: Find PRs where a user is mentioned in the discussion. Enter their exact username or use '@me' for yourself. GitHub usernames can only contain letters, numbers, and hyphens (no dots or other special characters). The user must exist on GitHub.

per_page.title: Per Page
per_page.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100). GitHub caps total search results at ~1000 items; iterate `page` until results fewer than `per_page` are returned, and add `repo`, `label`, or date filters when totals approach 1000.
per_page.human_parameter_description: How many results to show per page. Higher numbers return more results at once (up to 100).

is_merged.title: Is Merged
is_merged.description: Filter by merge status. True for merged PRs, False for unmerged, None for all.
is_merged.human_parameter_description: Filter for PRs that have been merged or not. Leave blank to include both.

base_branch.title: Base Branch
base_branch.human_parameter_description: Show PRs targeting a specific base branch (the branch being merged into), like 'main' or 'develop'.

head_branch.title: Head Branch
head_branch.human_parameter_description: Show PRs coming from a specific feature branch (the branch being merged), like 'feature/login'.

created_since.title: Created Since
created_since.description: Filter PRs created after this date (ISO 8601 format). Provide as UTC ISO 8601 timestamp to avoid off-by-one-day errors at range boundaries. Does not filter on `merged_at`.
created_since.human_parameter_description: Include only PRs opened on or after this date. Use ISO dates like '2024-01-01' or '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

updated_since.title: Updated Since
updated_since.description: Filter PRs updated after this date (ISO 8601 format).
updated_since.human_parameter_description: Include only PRs updated on or after this date. Use ISO dates like '2024-01-01' or '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

response_detail.title: Response Detail
response_detail.description: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) returns an optimized response for AI agents. 'full' returns the complete GitHub API response.
response_detail.human_parameter_description: Choose 'minimal' for a cleaner, AI-optimized summary, or 'full' for the complete GitHub API response.

for_authenticated_user.title: For Authenticated User
for_authenticated_user.description: Include private repositories accessible to the authenticated user in search results. When True without repo/owner, searches PRs involving you (author, assignee, mentions, commenter) across all accessible repos. When False without repo/owner, restricts to public repos only. When repo/owner is specified, this flag has no effect on scope. Set to True when searching private repositories; False searches all of GitHub and produces large noisy result sets.
for_authenticated_user.human_parameter_description: Turn this on to include private repositories you can access with your GitHub account. When no specific repo/owner is provided, this searches PRs where you're involved (author, assignee, mentioned, or commenter). Leave it off to search only public repositories.

name: Get a reference

input_parameters.title: GetAReferenceRequest

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: The Git reference to retrieve. Must be formatted as `heads/<branch_name>` for branches, `tags/<tag_name>` for tags, or `pull/<number>/head` (or `pull/<number>/merge`) for pull requests. Simple branch names (e.g., `main`) are automatically converted to `heads/<name>`. The reference must exist in the repository; a 404 error is returned if not found. If unsure which references exist, use 'list_matching_references' or 'get_a_branch' first. Note: Commit SHAs are not supported by this endpoint; use commit-specific endpoints instead. Not all repositories use 'master'; many now use 'main' as the default branch.
ref.human_parameter_description: The branch, tag, or pull request reference to retrieve. Format as 'heads/branch_name' for branches, 'tags/tag_name' for tags, or 'pull/number/head' for PRs. Simple names like 'main' are treated as branches and converted to 'heads/main'. The reference must exist (404 if not found). If unsure, list references first with 'list_matching_references'. Note: Commit SHAs are not supported by this endpoint.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: The name of the repository you want to get the reference from (without .git). This tells us which project under the owner to use.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: The GitHub account or organization that owns the repository you want to access. Enter the username (like 'octocat') or org name (like 'google') so we can find the right repo.

GetInteractionRestrictionsForAnOrganizat.description:
Response schema for `GetInteractionRestrictionsForAnOrganization`.

When interaction restrictions are active, the response contains:
- `limit`: The type of GitHub user allowed to interact. One of: `existing_users`, `contributors_only`, `collaborators_only`
- `origin`: The source of the restriction (e.g., "organization")
- `expires_at`: ISO 8601 timestamp when the restriction expires

Example (when restrictions are active):
```json
{
  "limit": "collaborators_only",
  "origin": "organization",
  "expires_at": "2018-08-17T04:18:39Z"
}
```

When no restrictions are set, the response is an empty object `{}`.

ref.title: Ref
ref.description: The name of the commit, branch, or tag to read from. Use this parameter to specify which branch (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main', 'develop'), tag (e.g., 'v1.2.0'), or commit SHA you want to access. If not provided, the repository's default branch will be used. Note: Branch names should be passed here, NOT in the path parameter.
ref.human_parameter_description: The branch, tag, or commit to read from. Use this to specify branches like 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main', or 'develop'. Leave empty to use the repository's default branch (often 'main'). IMPORTANT: Pass branch names here, not in the path parameter.

path.title: Path
path.description: Required. Path to file or directory in the repository. Empty string ('') retrieves root directory contents. Leading slashes auto-stripped. CRITICAL: Do NOT pass branch names here (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main'). Branch names belong in the `ref` parameter. Path should be file/directory path only (e.g., 'src/main.js', 'README.md'), NOT prefixed with branch name (use 'src/main.js' not 'main/src/main.js'). File paths must include extension (e.g., 'README.md', not 'README'). For common files (README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG) without extensions, action auto-tries common extensions (.md, .txt, .rst). Paths are case-sensitive. On 404 errors, list parent directory to verify exact path/casing.
path.human_parameter_description: The file or folder path inside the repository that you want to retrieve. Examples include 'README.md', 'src/main.js', or a directory like 'docs'. Use an empty string to list the root directory contents. Leading slashes are automatically removed. CRITICAL: Do NOT pass branch names here (like 'feat/something', 'main', 'develop'). To specify a branch, tag, or commit, use the `ref` parameter instead. The path should only contain the file/directory path within the repository. Do NOT include the branch name as a prefix - use 'README.md' not 'main/README.md'. Important: Include file extensions (e.g., 'README.md' not just 'README'). For common files like README, LICENSE, or CHANGELOG, the action will try common extensions automatically if not specified. Note: Paths are case-sensitive - 'Docker' and 'docker' are treated as different paths. If you get a 'Not Found' error, try listing the parent directory first to verify the exact path and casing.

page.title: Page
page.description: The page number of the results to fetch, used for pagination. Default is 1. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."
page.human_parameter_description: The page number of results to view. Use this to move forward or backward through paginated results.

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: REQUIRED. The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This is a path parameter needed to construct the API URL. This field is not case-sensitive.
repo.human_parameter_description: REQUIRED. The name of the repository you want to get issue comments from. This identifies which project to search. This field must be provided.

sort.title: SortEnm
sort.description: Specifies the field by which to sort the issue comments. Valid values are `created` (for creation date, default) or `updated` (for last update date).
sort.human_parameter_description: How you want the comments ordered: by when they were created or when they were last updated. Choose the option that matches how you prefer to review them.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: REQUIRED. The username of the account or the organization name that owns the repository. This is a path parameter needed to construct the API URL. This field is not case-sensitive.
owner.human_parameter_description: REQUIRED. The account or organization that owns the repository whose issue comments you want to list. Enter the GitHub username or organization name. This field must be provided.

since.title: Since
since.description: Filters comments to include only those last updated at or after the specified time. This should be a timestamp in ISO 8601 format (e.g., `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`).
since.human_parameter_description: Only include comments updated on or after this date and time to filter out older activity. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp, for example 2023-01-01T10:00:00Z.

per_page.title: Per Page
per_page.description: The number of issue comments to retrieve per page. Default is 30, maximum is 100. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."
per_page.human_parameter_description: How many comments to show per page of results. Higher numbers show more at once; lower numbers make pages shorter and faster to scan.

direction.title: DirectionEnm
direction.description: The direction for sorting results. Valid values are `asc` (ascending) or `desc` (descending). This parameter is effective only when `sort` is also specified.
direction.human_parameter_description: Whether to sort in ascending or descending order. Pick this to see newest or oldest comments first.

RemoveARepositoryFromAnAppInstallationRe.description:
Response for removing a repository from an app installation.

This endpoint returns an empty response body on success with HTTP status code 204 (No Content).
The successful removal of a repository from an app installation does not return any data fields.

Status codes:
- 204: No Content - Repository successfully removed from app installation. Response body is empty.
- 304: Not modified - Resource has not been modified since last request.
- 403: Forbidden - User lacks required admin access to the repository or the endpoint is being accessed with an unsupported token type.
- 404: Resource not found - The specified installation or repository does not exist, or the user does not have access.
- 422: Unprocessable Entity - Returned when the application is installed on all repositories in the organization, or if this request would remove the last repository that the application has access to in the organization.

Notes:
- This endpoint only works for PATs (classic) with the repo scope
- Does not work with GitHub App user access tokens, GitHub App installation access tokens, or fine-grained personal access tokens
- The authenticated user must have admin access to the repository
- The installation must have repository_selection of 'selected'

description: Tool to run an arbitrary GitHub GraphQL v4 query or mutation. Use when fetching multiple datasets in one batch. Cost-based rate limit: ~5,000 points/hour; keep field selections narrow, avoid deep nesting, and include rateLimit in responses to monitor quota. Responses are nested under data.data (e.g., data.data.repository.vulnerabilityAlerts); always inspect the errors array even on HTTP 200, as partial failures embed there. Paginate by looping on pageInfo.hasNextPage and advancing with pageInfo.endCursor. Search results cap at ~1,000 items per query; split by label, date range, or repository for full coverage. Use ProjectV2 nodes, not Classic Projects (deprecated). Parallel mutations (e.g., addProjectV2ItemById) can trigger transient conflicts; use sequential execution.

name: Search repositories

input_parameters.title: SearchRepositoriesRequest

q.title: Q
q.description: REQUIRED non-empty search query. Max 5 AND/OR/NOT operators. Qualifiers: `language:LANG`, `stars:N`, `stars:>N`, `forks:N`, `size:N` (KB), `topic:TOPIC`, `license:LICENSE`, `created:DATE`, `pushed:DATE`, `is:public|private`, `archived:true|false`, `in:name|description|readme`, `user:USERNAME`, `org:ORGNAME`. Must use real GitHub usernames/orgs (e.g., `user:octocat`), not placeholders. Queries with logical operators must include at least one plain keyword; `topic:solana OR topic:ethereum` fails, use `solana OR ethereum stars:>100` instead.
q.human_parameter_description: REQUIRED: Enter the words and filters that describe the repositories you want to find. This field must be provided and cannot be empty. You can include qualifiers like language, stars, or topic to narrow the results. To filter by user, provide an actual GitHub username (e.g., 'user:octocat'). IMPORTANT: Use at most 5 AND/OR/NOT operators in your query.

page.title: Page

sort.title: SortEnm

sort.human_parameter_description: Choose how the results should be sorted, such as by stars, forks, help-wanted issues, most recently updated, or creation date. Leave this blank to use GitHub's best match.

order.title: Order
order.description: Determines the order of search results: `desc` for descending or `asc` for ascending. This parameter is only effective when `sort` is also specified. Defaults to `desc`.
order.human_parameter_description: Pick whether the list should go from high to low or low to high. This only takes effect if you also choose a sort field.

name: Update branch protection

input_parameters.title: UpdateBranchProtectionRequest

repo.title: Repo
repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).
repo.human_parameter_description: The repository name you want to update, without the .git ending. This is the repo where the branch lives.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).
owner.human_parameter_description: The GitHub username or organization that owns the repository you want to update. Use the account name exactly as it appears on GitHub.

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: Name of the branch to protect; wildcard characters are not allowed (use GraphQL API for wildcard support).
branch.human_parameter_description: The exact name of the branch you want to protect, like 'main' or 'develop'. This tells us which branch’s rules to change.

lock_branch.title: Lock Branch
lock_branch.description: If `True`, sets the branch to read-only, preventing pushes.
lock_branch.human_parameter_description: Make the branch read-only so no one can push to it. Useful for freezing a branch.

enforce_admins.title: Enforce Admins
enforce_admins.description: Enforces configured restrictions for repository administrators. Set to `True` to enforce for admins, or `None`/`null` to disable.
enforce_admins.human_parameter_description: Choose whether these protection rules also apply to repository administrators.

allow_deletions.title: Allow Deletions
allow_deletions.description: Allows deletion of the protected branch.
allow_deletions.human_parameter_description: Allow the protected branch to be deleted. Keep off to prevent accidental deletions.

block_creations.title: Block Creations
block_creations.description: If `True`, push restrictions also apply to creating matching new branches, unless pusher has explicit push access.
block_creations.human_parameter_description: Also block the creation of new branches that match this rule unless the creator has push access. Use this to stop unauthorized branch creation.

allow_force_pushes.title: Allow Force Pushes
allow_force_pushes.description: Permits force pushes to the protected branch. Set to `True` to allow, `None`/`null` to block.
allow_force_pushes.human_parameter_description: Allow people to force push to the protected branch. Only enable this if you truly need to rewrite history.

allow_fork_syncing.title: Allow Fork Syncing
allow_fork_syncing.description: Allows users to pull upstream changes into their fork when the branch is locked.
allow_fork_syncing.human_parameter_description: Allow users to pull upstream changes into their forks even when the branch is locked. Helps keep forks up to date.

restrictions__apps.title: Restrictions  Apps
restrictions__apps.description: App `slug`s with push access. Cannot be used with `restrictions_users` or `restrictions_teams`. Empty list removes all.
restrictions__apps.human_parameter_description: Apps that are allowed to push directly to the protected branch. Leave empty to remove all app exceptions.

restrictions__teams.title: Restrictions  Teams
restrictions__teams.description: Team `slug`s with push access. Cannot be used with `restrictions_apps` or `restrictions_users`. Empty list removes all.
restrictions__teams.human_parameter_description: Team slugs that are allowed to push directly to the protected branch. Leave empty to remove all team exceptions.

restrictions__users.title: Restrictions  Users
restrictions__users.description: User `login`s with push access. Cannot be used with `restrictions_apps` or `restrictions_teams`. Empty list removes all.
restrictions__users.human_parameter_description: Usernames who are allowed to push directly to the protected branch. Leave empty to remove all user exceptions.

required_linear_history.title: Required Linear History
required_linear_history.description: Enforces linear commit history by preventing merge commits. Repository must allow squash or rebase merging.
required_linear_history.human_parameter_description: Prevent merge commits so the branch history stays linear. Use this to enforce squash or rebase workflows.

items.title: StatusCheck

app_id.description: The optional ID of the GitHub App that must provide this check.

required__status__checks__checks.title: Required  Status  Checks  Checks
required__status__checks__checks.description: List of status checks required to merge. Each check object needs a `context` string and optionally an `app_id` integer. **Mutually exclusive with `contexts`** - use one or the other, not both.
required__status__checks__checks.human_parameter_description: Use this to list the specific status checks that must pass before merging. Include the check name (context) and optionally the app that runs it.

required__status__checks__strict.title: Required  Status  Checks  Strict
required__status__checks__strict.description: Require branches to be up to date with the base branch before merging; if `True`, merges are blocked if the head branch is behind the base branch.
required__status__checks__strict.human_parameter_description: Choose whether the branch must be fully up to date with the base branch before it can be merged. Turn this on to prevent merging when the branch is behind.

required_conversation_resolution.title: Required Conversation Resolution
required_conversation_resolution.description: Requires all conversations on code to be resolved before merging a pull request.
required_conversation_resolution.human_parameter_description: Require all review discussions to be resolved before merging. Ensures feedback is addressed before changes go in.

required__status__checks__contexts.title: Required  Status  Checks  Contexts
required__status__checks__contexts.description: **Deprecated**: List of status check contexts required to merge. If set by a GitHub App, future checks must come from that app. Use `checks` for finer control. **Mutually exclusive with `checks`** - use one or the other, not both.
required__status__checks__contexts.human_parameter_description: Names of the status checks that must pass before merging (for example, your CI or lint jobs).

required__pull__request__reviews__dismis.title: Required  Pull  Request  Reviews  Dismiss  Stale  Reviews
required__pull__request__reviews__dismis.description: If `True`, new commits dismiss previous review approvals on a pull request branch.
required__pull__request__reviews__dismis.human_parameter_description: Automatically dismiss approvals when new commits are pushed so reviewers must re-approve the latest changes.

required__pull_request__reviews__approvi.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Approving  Review  Count
required__pull_request__reviews__approvi.description: Number of approving reviews (0-6) required to merge a pull request; 0 disables.
required__pull_request__reviews__approvi.human_parameter_description: How many approving reviews are required before merging. Set to 0 to disable the approval requirement.

required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Bypass  Allowances  Apps
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.description: App `slug`s allowed to bypass pull request requirements. Empty list removes all.
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.human_parameter_name: Apps allowed to bypass pull request requirements
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.human_parameter_description: Apps that may bypass pull request requirements. Grant only to trusted automation.

required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Bypass  Allowances  Teams
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.description: Team `slug`s allowed to bypass pull request requirements. Empty list removes all.
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.human_parameter_name: Teams allowed to bypass pull request requirements
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.human_parameter_description: Team slugs allowed to merge without meeting all pull request requirements. Use for trusted teams.

required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Bypass  Allowances  Users
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.description: User `login`s allowed to bypass pull request requirements. Empty list removes all.
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.human_parameter_name: Users allowed to bypass pull request requirements
required__pull_request__reviews__bypass_.human_parameter_description: Usernames who are allowed to merge without meeting all pull request requirements. Use sparingly for trusted users.

required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Dismiss  Restrictions  Apps
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.description: App `slug`s allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Empty list removes all.
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.human_parameter_description: App slugs that are allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Useful for approved automation tools.

required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Dismiss  Restrictions  Teams
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.description: Team `slug`s allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Empty list removes all.
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.human_parameter_description: Team slugs who are allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Use this to grant override ability to trusted teams.

required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Dismiss  Restrictions  Users
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.description: User `login`s allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Empty list removes all.
required__pull_request__reviews__dismiss.human_parameter_description: Usernames who are allowed to dismiss pull request reviews. Add trusted people who can override reviews when needed.

required__pull_request__reviews__require.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Require  Code  Owner  Reviews

required__pull_request__reviews__require.human_parameter_description: Require approval from code owners when their files are changed. Ensures the right people review sensitive areas.

required__pull_request__reviews__require.title: Required  Pull Request  Reviews  Require  Last  Push  Approval
required__pull_request__reviews__require.description: If `True`, the most recent push must be approved by someone other than the pusher.

message_id.description: Immutable ID of the message to modify. Gmail message IDs are hexadecimal strings (e.g., '1a2b3c4d5e6f7890'). IMPORTANT: Do NOT use UUIDs (32-character strings like '093ca4662b214d5eba8f4ceeaad63433'), thread IDs, or internal system IDs - these will cause 'Invalid id value' errors. Obtain valid message IDs from: (1) 'GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS' response 'messageId' field, (2) 'GMAIL_FETCH_MESSAGE_BY_THREAD_ID' response, or (3) 'GMAIL_LIST_THREADS' and then fetching thread messages.
message_id.human_parameter_description: Enter the Gmail message ID (a hexadecimal string like '1a2b3c4d5e6f7890'). Get this from GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS 'messageId' field. Do NOT use UUIDs or 32-character strings.

add_label_ids.title: Add Label Ids
add_label_ids.description: Label IDs to add (IDs, not display names). System labels: INBOX, SPAM, TRASH, UNREAD, STARRED, IMPORTANT, CATEGORY_PERSONAL, CATEGORY_SOCIAL, CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS, CATEGORY_UPDATES, CATEGORY_FORUMS. Use full CATEGORY_ prefix (e.g., 'CATEGORY_UPDATES' not 'UPDATES'). Custom labels: call 'listLabels' first to get the ID (format: 'Label_<number>'). Do NOT use the label display name; the API requires the ID. SENT, DRAFT, CHAT are immutable and cannot be added or removed. A label cannot appear in both add_label_ids and remove_label_ids.
add_label_ids.human_parameter_description: List the IDs of labels to add. Use exact system label IDs (e.g., 'CATEGORY_UPDATES' not 'UPDATES') or custom label IDs from listLabels (e.g., 'Label_1' not the label name). Note: SENT, DRAFT, and CHAT cannot be modified.

remove_label_ids.title: Remove Label Ids
remove_label_ids.description: Label IDs to remove (IDs, not display names). System labels: INBOX, SPAM, TRASH, UNREAD, STARRED, IMPORTANT, CATEGORY_PERSONAL, CATEGORY_SOCIAL, CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS, CATEGORY_UPDATES, CATEGORY_FORUMS. Use full CATEGORY_ prefix (e.g., 'CATEGORY_UPDATES' not 'UPDATES'). Custom labels: call 'listLabels' first to get the ID (format: 'Label_<number>'). SENT, DRAFT, CHAT are immutable and cannot be removed. Common operations: to mark as read, remove 'UNREAD'; to archive, remove 'INBOX'. A label cannot appear in both add_label_ids and remove_label_ids.
remove_label_ids.human_parameter_description: List the IDs of labels to remove. Use exact system label IDs (e.g., 'CATEGORY_UPDATES' not 'UPDATES') or custom label IDs from listLabels (e.g., 'Label_1' not the label name). To mark as read, remove 'UNREAD'. addLabelIds.title: Add Label Ids
addLabelIds.description: List of label IDs to add to the messages. IMPORTANT: Use label IDs, NOT label display names. System labels use their name as ID: INBOX, STARRED, IMPORTANT, SENT, DRAFT, SPAM, TRASH, UNREAD, CATEGORY_PERSONAL, CATEGORY_SOCIAL, CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS, CATEGORY_UPDATES, CATEGORY_FORUMS. Custom labels MUST use their ID (format: 'Label_XXX', e.g., 'Label_1', 'Label_25'), NOT the display name (e.g., do NOT use 'Work' or 'Projects'). Call GMAIL_LIST_LABELS first to get the 'id' field for custom labels. At least one of add_label_ids or remove_label_ids must be provided. CONSTRAINT: Label IDs must NOT overlap with remove_label_ids - cannot add and remove the same label.
addLabelIds.human_parameter_description: Specify the label IDs you want to add. For system labels use INBOX, STARRED, etc. For custom labels, first call GMAIL_LIST_LABELS to get the label ID (format: Label_XXX).

removeLabelIds.title: Remove Label Ids
removeLabelIds.description: List of label IDs to remove from the messages. IMPORTANT: Use label IDs, NOT label display names. System labels use their name as ID: INBOX, STARRED, IMPORTANT, SENT, SPAM, TRASH, UNREAD. Custom labels MUST use their ID (format: 'Label_XXX', e.g., 'Label_1', 'Label_25'), NOT the display name (e.g., do NOT use 'Work' or 'Projects'). Call GMAIL_LIST_LABELS first to get the 'id' field for custom labels. Common use cases: Remove 'UNREAD' to mark as read, remove 'INBOX' to archive. Note: 'DRAFT' cannot be removed - use GMAIL_DELETE_DRAFT instead. At least one of add_label_ids or remove_label_ids must be provided. label_name.title: Label Name
label_name.description: REQUIRED. The name for the new label. Must be unique within the account, non-blank, maximum length 225 characters, cannot contain commas (','), not only whitespace, and must not be a reserved system label. Reserved English system labels include: Inbox, Starred, Important, Sent, Draft, Drafts, Spam, Trash, etc. Forward slashes ('/') are allowed and used to create hierarchical nested labels (e.g., 'Work/Projects', 'Personal/Finance'). When creating nested labels, any missing parent labels will be automatically created (similar to 'mkdir -p'). Periods ('.') are allowed and commonly used for numbering schemes (e.g., '1. Action Items', '2. Projects'). Note: 'name' is also accepted as an alias for this field. If a label with this name already exists, returns a 409 conflict; use GMAIL_LIST_LABELS to check existing labels and reuse the existing labelId, or use GMAIL_PATCH_LABEL to update it.

text_color.title: GmailLabelColor
text_color.description: Text color for the label. Gmail only accepts colors from a predefined palette of 102 specific hex values. Common color names like 'YELLOW', 'RED', 'BLUE', 'GREEN', 'ORANGE', 'PURPLE', 'PINK' are automatically mapped to the closest Gmail palette color. Provide either a common color name, a Gmail palette color name (e.g., 'BLACK', 'ROYAL_BLUE'), or exact hex value (e.g., '#000000', '#4a86e8'). If only text_color is provided without background_color, a complementary background color (white or black) will be auto-selected for optimal contrast. Full palette: https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.labels#Color Must be supplied together with background_color — providing only one will cause a 400 error. The auto-selected complementary color behavior does not apply; both colors are required.
text_color.human_parameter_description: Pick a color for the label text. Common names like 'YELLOW', 'RED', 'BLUE', 'GREEN' are automatically mapped to Gmail palette colors.

If only background_color is provided without text_color, a complementary text color (white or black) will be auto-selected for optimal contrast. Full palette: https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.labels#Color Must be supplied together with text_color — providing only one will cause a 400 error. query.title: Query
query.description: Gmail advanced search query (e.g., 'from:user subject:meeting'). Supported operators: 'from:', 'to:', 'subject:', 'label:', 'has:', 'is:', 'in:', 'category:', 'after:YYYY/MM/DD', 'before:YYYY/MM/DD', AND/OR/NOT. IMPORTANT - 'is:' vs 'label:' usage: Use 'is:' for special mail states: is:snoozed, is:unread, is:read, is:starred, is:important. Use 'label:' ONLY for user-created labels (e.g., 'label:work', 'label:projects'). Note: 'muted' may work with both 'is:muted' and 'label:muted' based on community reports. Common mistake: 'label:snoozed' is WRONG - use 'is:snoozed' instead. Use quotes for exact phrases. Omit for no query filter. after:/before: evaluate whole calendar days in UTC; before: is exclusive — adjust for local timezone to avoid off-by-one-day gaps.
query.human_parameter_description: Input a search term to filter your emails. Use 'is:' for special states (is:snoozed, is:unread, is:read, is:starred, is:important). Use 'label:' only for user-created labels (exception: 'muted' may work with both).

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user. Non-'me' addresses require domain-level delegation; without it, authentication or not-found errors result.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the email address of the user whose mailbox you want to access. You can use 'me' to refer to your own mailbox.

verbose.title: Verbose
verbose.description: If false, uses optimized concurrent metadata fetching for faster performance (~75% improvement). If true, uses standard detailed message fetching. When false, only essential fields (subject, sender, recipient, time, labels) are guaranteed. Body content and attachment details require verbose=true even when include_payload=true.
verbose.human_parameter_description: Select this to get detailed information for each email or to speed up the process and get just the basics.

ids_only.title: Ids Only
ids_only.description: If true, only returns message IDs from the list API without fetching individual message details. Fastest option for getting just message IDs and thread IDs.
ids_only.human_parameter_description: Use this option if you just want the IDs of emails without loading their full details, making the request quicker.

label_ids.title: Label Ids
label_ids.description: Filter by label IDs; only messages with all specified labels are returned (AND logic). Optional - omit or use empty list to fetch all messages without label filtering. System label IDs: 'INBOX', 'SPAM', 'TRASH', 'UNREAD', 'STARRED', 'IMPORTANT', 'CATEGORY_PRIMARY' (alias 'CATEGORY_PERSONAL'), 'CATEGORY_SOCIAL', 'CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS', 'CATEGORY_UPDATES', 'CATEGORY_FORUMS'. For custom/user-created labels, you MUST use the label ID (e.g., 'Label_123456'), NOT the display name. Use the 'listLabels' action to find label IDs for custom labels. Combining label_ids with label: in query applies AND logic across both, which can silently over-restrict results; use one strategy consistently.
label_ids.human_parameter_description: List the label IDs to filter which messages to fetch. System labels (INBOX, SPAM, etc.) can be used directly by name. For custom labels, you must use the listLabels action first to get the label ID - do not use the label name you see in Gmail.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Token for retrieving a specific page, obtained from a previous response's `nextPageToken`. Must be a valid opaque token string from a previous API response. Do not pass arbitrary values. Omit for the first page. Loop calls using nextPageToken until it is absent to avoid silently missing messages. resultSizeEstimate is approximate — do not use as a stopping condition.
page_token.human_parameter_description: If you've paginated results, use this token to get the next set of messages. Leave blank for the first page.

max_results.title: Max Results
max_results.description: Maximum number of messages to retrieve per page. Default of 1 retrieves only a single message; set higher for practical use. Hard cap is 500 per page.
max_results.human_parameter_description: Specify how many email messages you want to retrieve in one request, from 1 to 500.

include_payload.title: Include Payload
include_payload.description: Set to true to include full message payload (headers, body, attachments); false for metadata only. payload may still be null even when true; use GMAIL_FETCH_MESSAGE_BY_MESSAGE_ID for guaranteed complete content. When payload is present, bodies are base64url-encoded in payload.parts; replace '-'→'+' and '_'→'/' and fix padding before decoding, and check both text/plain and text/html parts.
include_payload.human_parameter_description: Choose whether to get the full content of each email, including attachments and body, or just the essential metadata.

include_spam_trash.title: Include Spam Trash
include_spam_trash.description: Set to true to include messages from 'SPAM' and 'TRASH'.
include_spam_trash.human_parameter_description: Decide if you want to see emails that are normally filtered into your SPAM or TRASH folders.

description: Retrieves all system and user-created labels for a Gmail account in a single unpaginated response. Primary use: obtain internal label IDs (e.g., 'Label_123') required by other Gmail tools — display names cannot be used as label identifiers and cause silent failures or errors. System labels (INBOX, UNREAD, SPAM, TRASH, etc.) are case-sensitive and must be used exactly as returned; INBOX, SPAM, and TRASH are read-only and cannot be added/removed via label modification tools. The Gmail search 'label:' operator accepts display names, but label_ids parameters in tools like GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS require internal IDs from this tool — mixing conventions yields zero results silently. Do not hardcode label IDs across sessions; refresh via this tool on conflict errors.

add_label_ids.title: Add Label Ids
add_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to add to the thread. Must be valid label IDs that exist in the user's account. System labels use uppercase names (e.g., 'INBOX', 'STARRED', 'IMPORTANT', 'UNREAD', 'SPAM', 'TRASH', 'SENT', 'DRAFT', 'CATEGORY_PERSONAL', 'CATEGORY_SOCIAL', 'CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS', 'CATEGORY_UPDATES', 'CATEGORY_FORUMS'). Custom labels use the format 'Label_N' (e.g., 'Label_1', 'Label_42'). Use GMAIL_LIST_LABELS to discover available label IDs. Accepts either a list or a JSON-encoded string. Note: If a label appears in both add_label_ids and remove_label_ids, the add operation takes priority. Use GMAIL_CREATE_LABEL first if the label does not yet exist, then supply its returned ID here.
add_label_ids.human_parameter_description: Provide the labels you want to apply to the thread. Use GMAIL_LIST_LABELS to find valid label IDs.

remove_label_ids.title: Remove Label Ids
remove_label_ids.description: List of label IDs to remove from the thread. Must be valid label IDs that exist in the user's account. System labels use uppercase names (e.g., 'INBOX', 'STARRED', 'IMPORTANT', 'UNREAD', 'SPAM', 'TRASH', 'SENT', 'DRAFT', 'CATEGORY_PERSONAL', 'CATEGORY_SOCIAL', 'CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS', 'CATEGORY_UPDATES', 'CATEGORY_FORUMS'). Custom labels use the format 'Label_N' (e.g., 'Label_1', 'Label_42'). Use GMAIL_LIST_LABELS to discover available label IDs. Accepts either a list or a JSON-encoded string. Note: Labels that appear in both add_label_ids and remove_label_ids will be automatically removed from this list (add takes priority).
remove_label_ids.human_parameter_description: Specify the labels you want to remove from the thread. Use GMAIL_LIST_LABELS to find valid label IDs.

deletionTime.description: Output only. The time the user's account was deleted. The value is in ISO 8601 date and time format. The time is the complete date plus hours, minutes, and seconds in the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssTZD. For example, 2010-04-05T17:30:04+01:00.

hashFunction.title: Hash Function
hashFunction.description: Stores the hash format of the password property. The following hashFunction values are allowed: MD5, SHA-1, and crypt. We recommend administrators use the crypt hash function.

primaryEmail.title: Primary Email
primaryEmail.description: The user's primary email address. This property is required in a request to create a user account. The primaryEmail must be unique and cannot be an alias of another user.

agreedToTerms.title: Agreed To Terms
agreedToTerms.description: Output only. This property is true if the user has completed an initial login and accepted the Terms of Service agreement.

customSchemas.title: Custom Schemas
customSchemas.description: Custom fields of the user. The key is a schema_name and its values are 'fieldname': 'field_value'.

ipWhitelisted.title: Ip Whitelisted
ipWhitelisted.description: If true, the user's IP address is subject to a deprecated IP address allowlist configuration.

lastLoginTime.title: Last Login Time
lastLoginTime.description: Output only. The last time the user logged into the user's account. The value is in ISO 8601 date and time format. The time is the complete date plus hours, minutes, and seconds in the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssTZD. For example, 2010-04-05T17:30:04+01:00.

organizations.title: Organizations
organizations.description: A list of organizations the user belongs to. The maximum allowed data size for this field is 10KB.

posixAccounts.title: Posix Accounts
posixAccounts.description: The list of POSIX account information for the user.

recoveryPhone.title: Recovery Phone
recoveryPhone.description: Recovery phone of the user. The phone number must be in the E.164 format, starting with the plus sign (+). Example: +16506661212.

sshPublicKeys.title: Ssh Public Keys
sshPublicKeys.description: A list of SSH public keys.

isMailboxSetup.title: Is Mailbox Setup
isMailboxSetup.description: Output only. Indicates if the user's Google mailbox is created. This property is only applicable if the user has been assigned a Gmail license.

isEnrolledIn2Sv.title: Is Enrolled In2 Sv
isEnrolledIn2Sv.description: Output only. Is enrolled in 2-step verification.

isDelegatedAdmin.title: Is Delegated Admin
isDelegatedAdmin.description: Output only. Indicates if the user is a delegated administrator.

suspensionReason.title: Suspension Reason
suspensionReason.description: Output only. Has the reason a user account is suspended either by the administrator or by Google at the time of suspension. The property is returned only if the suspended property is true.

thumbnailPhotoUrl.title: Thumbnail Photo Url

nonEditableAliases.title: Non Editable Aliases
nonEditableAliases.description: Output only. A list of the user's non-editable alias email addresses. These are typically outside the account's primary domain or sub-domain.

thumbnailPhotoEtag.title: Thumbnail Photo Etag

changePasswordAtNextLogin.title: Change Password At Next Login

name: Run Report

input_parameters.title: RunReportRequest

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Optional. Number of rows to return. Must be between 1 and 250000.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Optional. 0-based start row for pagination. Must be >= 0.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: Optional. The metrics to request and display. Maximum 10 metrics per request. Each metric MUST be an object with a required non-empty 'name' field. Common valid metric names: activeUsers, totalUsers, newUsers, sessions, engagedSessions, screenPageViews, eventCount, conversions, userEngagementDuration, engagementRate, bounceRate, averageSessionDuration, sessionsPerUser, screenPageViewsPerSession, purchaseRevenue, totalRevenue, transactions, ecommercePurchases, publisherAdClicks, publisherAdImpressions, totalAdRevenue. Custom metrics use format 'customEvent:parameter_name'. CRITICAL: 'averageEngagementTime' is NOT a valid metric - use 'userEngagementDuration' or 'averageSessionDuration' instead. 'exits' is NOT a valid metric in GA4.

orderBys.title: Order Bys
orderBys.description: Optional. Specify how rows are ordered. Each OrderBy object must have 'desc' (boolean) at the top level and exactly one of: 'metric' (with 'metricName' string), 'dimension' (with 'dimensionName' or 'name' string and optional 'orderType': 'ALPHANUMERIC', 'CASE_INSENSITIVE_ALPHANUMERIC', or 'NUMERIC'), or 'pivot'. Note: For dimension ordering, you can use either 'dimensionName' or 'name' field - both are accepted and normalized. Example for metric ordering: {'desc': true, 'metric': {'metricName': 'activeUsers'}}. Example for dimension ordering: {'desc': false, 'dimension': {'dimensionName': 'country', 'orderType': 'ALPHANUMERIC'}}.

property.title: Property
property.description: Required. The property resource on which to run the report. Format: properties/{property_id} where property_id must be a numeric ID (e.g., 'properties/123456789').

cohortSpec.title: Cohort Spec
cohortSpec.description: Optional. Cohort specification. Requires requesting the cohort dimension.

dateRanges.title: Date Ranges
dateRanges.description: The date ranges to read. Required for standard reports. Each range MUST be an object with required 'startDate' and 'endDate' fields (both must be non-empty). Dates can be in YYYY-MM-DD format or special values like 'today', 'yesterday', '7daysAgo', '30daysAgo'. IMPORTANT: For cohort requests (when cohortSpec is provided), dateRanges must be omitted.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.description: Optional. The dimensions to request and display. Maximum 9 dimensions per request. Each dimension MUST be an object with a required non-empty 'name' field. Common valid dimension names: date, dateHour, dateHourMinute, year, month, week, day, dayOfWeek, hour, city, cityId, country, countryId, continent, continentId, region, subContinent, deviceCategory, browser, operatingSystem, platform, platformDeviceCategory, screenResolution, sessionSource, sessionMedium, sessionSourceMedium, sessionCampaignName, sessionDefaultChannelGroup, firstUserSource, firstUserMedium, firstUserCampaignName, firstUserDefaultChannelGroup, pagePath, pagePathPlusQueryString, pageTitle, landingPage, hostname, eventName, streamName, userAgeBracket, userGender, language, newVsReturning. Custom dimensions: 'customEvent:parameter_name' or 'customUser:parameter_name'. 'dateRange' is NOT a valid dimension — use date dimensions (date, dateHour, year, month, etc.) instead. 'exits' is NOT a valid dimension in GA4. COMPATIBILITY: Not all dimensions can be combined with each other or with certain metrics/filters. If you receive a compatibility error, use GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_CHECK_COMPATIBILITY to validate combinations, or see https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/compatibility

comparisons.title: Comparisons
comparisons.description: Optional. The comparison configuration. Adds a comparison column to the response.

currencyCode.title: Currency Code
currencyCode.description: Optional. The currency code to apply, in ISO 4217 format. Defaults to property currency.

metricFilter.title: Metric Filter
metricFilter.description: Optional. Filter expression to restrict rows by metric values. Applied after aggregation. IMPORTANT: Only use metric field names here (e.g., 'activeUsers', 'sessions', 'ecommercePurchases', 'purchaseRevenue'). Do NOT use dimension names in metricFilter - if you need to filter by a dimension (e.g., 'country', 'city', 'pagePath'), use dimensionFilter instead. The action validates that only metric names are used in metricFilter and will reject dimension names with a clear error. Structure: {'filter': {'fieldName': '<metric_name>', 'numericFilter': {'operation': 'GREATER_THAN', 'value': {'int64Value': '0'}}}} or use 'andGroup'/'orGroup' for multiple conditions.

keepEmptyRows.title: Keep Empty Rows
keepEmptyRows.description: Optional. If true, rows with all zero metrics will be returned; otherwise omitted.

dimensionFilter.title: Dimension Filter
dimensionFilter.description: Optional. Filter expression to restrict rows by dimension values. IMPORTANT: Only use dimension field names here (e.g., 'country', 'city', 'date', 'deviceCategory', 'pagePath'). Do NOT use metric names in dimensionFilter - if you need to filter by a metric (e.g., 'activeUsers', 'sessions', 'ecommercePurchases'), use metricFilter instead. Structure: {'filter': {'fieldName': '<dimension_name>', 'stringFilter': {...}}} or use 'andGroup'/'orGroup' for multiple conditions. COMPATIBILITY WARNING: Dimension filters must be compatible with the dimensions in your request. For example, filtering on 'sessionCampaignName' while using demographic dimensions (userAgeBracket, userGender) will fail. The filter field creates an implicit dimension that must be compatible with all other dimensions and metrics. Use GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_CHECK_COMPATIBILITY to verify your filter dimensions work with your requested dimensions/metrics.

metricAggregations.title: Metric Aggregations
metricAggregations.description: Optional. Aggregation types to include over metrics, e.g., 'TOTAL', 'MINIMUM', 'MAXIMUM'.

returnPropertyQuota.title: Return Property Quota

anchor.title: Anchor
anchor.description: A JSON string defining the region of the document to which the comment is anchored. Format: {"region": {"kind": "drive#commentRegion", "<classifier>": <value>, "rev": "head"}}. Supported classifiers: (1) "line" for text lines (e.g., "line": 12), (2) "page" for page numbers (e.g., "page": {"p": 0}), (3) "txt" for text ranges (e.g., "txt": {"o": 100, "l": 50}), (4) "rect" for rectangles in images (e.g., "rect": {"x": 10, "y": 20, "w": 100, "h": 50}), (5) "time" for video timestamps (e.g., "time": {"t": "00:01:30"}), (6) "matrix" for spreadsheet cells (e.g., "matrix": {"c": 2, "r": 5}). Note: On blob files, only unanchored comments are supported. Google Workspace editors may treat API-set anchors as unanchored.
anchor.human_parameter_description: Optional: A JSON string specifying the region in the document to anchor the comment to. Use different classifiers for different file types: 'line' for text documents, 'page' for PDFs, 'matrix' for spreadsheets, 'rect' for images, 'time' for videos, or 'txt' for text ranges. Note: Anchors may not display correctly in Google Workspace editors.

description: Creates a new file or folder in Google Drive. Supports both metadata-only creation (for folders and empty documents) and file upload with content. When file_to_upload is provided, uploads the actual file bytes; otherwise creates an empty file. Native Google file types (Docs, Sheets, Forms, etc.) and folders are created as empty shells when no content is provided; content must be added manually afterward. Newly created files are private by default — set sharing permissions afterward for collaboration. For shared-drive folders, use this tool with the target folder ID in `parents` rather than GOOGLEDRIVE_CREATE_FOLDER.

mime_type.title: Mime Type
mime_type.description: MIME type for the new file, determining how Google Drive interprets its content. Must exactly match the content type — a mismatched value (e.g., `text/plain` for HTML) breaks Drive previews and downstream conversion.

parent_id.title: Parent Id

If omitted, the file is created in the root of 'My Drive'. To get a folder ID from a folder name, use GOOGLEDRIVE_FIND_FOLDER first. Also accepts 'folder_id' or 'parent_folder_id' as aliases.
parent_id.human_parameter_description: The folder where you want the file to be created. Leave this blank to save it to My Drive. IMPORTANT: You must provide a valid folder ID (not folder name). Use GOOGLEDRIVE_FIND_FOLDER to get the folder ID if you only know the folder name.

text_content.title: Text Content
text_content.description: Required. Plain text content to be written into the new file. Also accepts 'content', 'body', or 'text' as aliases. Only the documented aliases (`content`, `body`, `text`) are accepted; undocumented keys like `file_content` cause an 'Invalid request data' error. Must be UTF-8 encoded.

type.title: Type
type.description: The type of the grantee. When creating a permission, if type is 'user' or 'group', you must provide an emailAddress. When type is 'domain', you must provide a domain. There isn't extra information required for 'anyone' type.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: The domain to which this permission refers. Required when type is 'domain'.

file_id.description: The ID of the file or shared drive.

email_address.title: Email Address
email_address.description: The email address of the user or group to which this permission refers. Required when type is 'user' or 'group'.

expiration_time.description: The time at which this permission will expire (RFC 3339 date-time). Expiration times can only be set on user and group permissions, must be in the future, and cannot be more than a year in the future.

transfer_ownership.description: Whether to transfer ownership to the specified user and downgrade the current owner to a writer. This parameter is required as an acknowledgement of the side effect.

name: Find file

q.title: Q
examples: name contains 'report' and not name contains 'draft'
name contains 'invoice' and modifiedTime > '2024-01-01T00:00:00' and trashed = false
q.description:
Query string to filter file results. Accepts both simple text searches and full Google Drive query syntax.

        **Simple Text Search:** Bare text (e.g., "SAM RFP") is auto-converted to fullText search. Bare email addresses are auto-converted to owner search.

        **Full Query Syntax:** 'field operator value' combined with 'and', 'or', 'not'

        **Operators:** =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, contains, in

        **Common Fields:**
        - `name` - File name (exact match with = or partial match with contains)
        - `fullText` - File content search
        - `mimeType` - File type (e.g., 'application/pdf', 'application/vnd.google-apps.folder')
        - `modifiedTime`, `createdTime` - Dates (RFC 3339: '2024-01-01T00:00:00')
        - `parents` - Folder IDs containing the file
        - `owners`, `writers` - User email addresses (MUST use 'in' operator, NOT colon syntax)
        - `properties`, `appProperties` - Custom metadata

        **Boolean Filter Fields (sharedWithMe, trashed, starred):**
        These fields require explicit `= true` or `= false` syntax:
        - `sharedWithMe = true` - Find files shared with you by others
        - `sharedWithMe = false` - Find files NOT shared with you (your own files)
        - `trashed = true` - Find files in trash
        - `trashed = false` - Exclude trashed files from results
        - `starred = true` - Find starred/favorited files
        - `starred = false` - Find non-starred files

        Combine with other conditions using 'and':
        - "sharedWithMe = true and name contains 'report'" - Find shared files with 'report' in name
        - "sharedWithMe = true and mimeType = 'application/pdf'" - Find shared PDF files
        - "starred = true and modifiedTime > '2024-01-01T00:00:00'" - Find recently modified starred files

        **Query Complexity Limits:**
        Queries with many OR clauses (typically >5-10) may fail with 'The query is too complex' error.

        **Name Field Usage:**
        Wildcards (*) are NOT supported. Use 'contains' operator for partial matching.

        **User Email Searches:**
        - CORRECT: "'user@example.com' in owners" or "'user@example.com' in writers" or "'user@example.com' in readers"
        - INCORRECT: "owner:user@example.com" (colon syntax is NOT supported and will cause errors)
        - Always use the 'in' operator with quoted email addresses for user-based searches

        **Special Syntax:**
        - Dates: RFC 3339 format (time zone defaults to UTC)
        - Apostrophes/quotes in values: Automatically escaped. You can write "name = 'Jan'26'" or "name = 'Valentine's Day'" without manual escaping.
        - Grouping: Use parentheses for OR: "(mimeType contains 'image/' or mimeType contains 'video/')"
        - Custom properties: "properties has { key='department' and value='sales' }"

        **IMPORTANT - Root Folder ('My Drive'):**
        'My Drive' is NOT a searchable folder name. To work with the root folder, use the 'root' alias: folder_id='root' or "'root' in parents" in your query.
q.human_parameter_description: Write a search filter to find the files you want, like name contains 'report' or modifiedTime > '2024-01-01'. Use this to narrow results to exactly what you need.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description:
Selector specifying which fields to include in a partial response. Use '*' for all fields.

**Default Behavior (Recommended for Discovery):**
When omitted, returns essential file discovery fields: id, name, mimeType, size, modifiedTime, createdTime, parents, webViewLink, trashed, starred. This lightweight default is optimized for file search/discovery use cases without verbose permission or capability metadata.

**Format:** For file fields, use 'files(field1,field2,...)' format. For example: 'files(id,name,mimeType)'.
Top-level response fields (kind, nextPageToken, incompleteSearch) can be used directly.

**Note:** Bare field names like 'id,name,mimeType' will be automatically wrapped in 'files()' for convenience.
The 'editors' field is not valid in Drive API v3; use 'permissions' instead for access control information.
fields.human_parameter_description: Choose which fields to return in the results. Omit for lightweight discovery defaults (id, name, mimeType, size, modifiedTime, etc.). Use '*' for all fields or list specific fields like 'id,name,mimeType' (will be auto-wrapped in 'files()'). For permission info, use 'permissions' not 'editors'.

spaces.title: Spaces
spaces.description: A comma-separated list of spaces to query. Supported values are 'drive', 'appDataFolder' and 'photos'.
spaces.human_parameter_description: Limit the search to certain Google Drive spaces like 'drive', 'appDataFolder', or 'photos'. Use this to focus on the right area.

corpora.title: Corpora
corpora.description:
Specifies which collections of files to search. Defaults to 'allDrives' (searches My Drive + all accessible shared drives).

        **Values:**
        - `user` - Search only user's personal My Drive
        - `domain` - Search all files shared within Google Workspace domain
        - `drive` - Search specific shared drive (requires 'driveId' parameter and 'includeItemsFromAllDrives' must be true)
        - `allDrives` - Search My Drive + all accessible shared drives (DEFAULT, requires 'includeItemsFromAllDrives' to be true)

        **When to Use:**
        - Personal files only: Use 'user'
        - Organization-wide: Use 'domain'
        - Specific shared drive: Use 'drive' with 'driveId'
        - Maximum coverage: Use 'allDrives' (auto-enables supportsAllDrives and includeItemsFromAllDrives)
corpora.human_parameter_description: Choose where to search (your drive, a shared drive, your whole domain, or all drives) so the results come from the right place. Defaults to 'allDrives' for comprehensive results.

driveId.title: Drive Id
driveId.description: ID of the shared drive to search. When provided, 'corpora' will automatically be set to 'drive' (mutually exclusive with corpora='allDrives'). Required if 'corpora' is 'drive'.
driveId.human_parameter_description: If you selected a specific shared drive, enter its ID so the search runs only within that drive.

orderBy.title: Order By
orderBy.description:
Comma-separated sort keys. Ascending by default; add 'desc' for descending. Cannot be used when query (q) contains fullText search terms.

        **Valid Keys:**
        - `createdTime`, `modifiedTime`, `modifiedByMeTime` - Dates
        - `viewedByMeTime`, `sharedWithMeTime` - Activity dates
        - `name`, `name_natural` - File name (natural: file1, file2, file10)
        - `folder` - Folder hierarchy
        - `quotaBytesUsed` - Storage size (NOTE: 'size' is NOT valid, use 'quotaBytesUsed')
        - `starred` - Starred status
        - `recency` - Recent activity (combines view time and modification time for relevance-based sorting)

        **Important:** 'size' is NOT a valid sort key. Use 'quotaBytesUsed' to sort by file size.

        **Restriction:** Sorting is not supported when the query contains fullText searches (e.g., "fullText contains 'keyword'"). Omit orderBy when using fullText queries.
orderBy.human_parameter_description: Pick how results should be sorted (e.g., by name or modified time). Add 'desc' for newest or largest first. Use 'quotaBytesUsed' for size sorting (not 'size'). Note: cannot be used with fullText searches.

description: The comprehensive Google Drive search tool that handles all file and folder discovery needs. Use this for any file finding task - from simple name searches to complex queries with date filters, MIME types, permissions, custom properties, folder scoping, and more. Searches across My Drive and shared drives with full metadata support. Examples: - Find PDFs: q="mimeType = 'application/pdf'" - Find recent files: q="modifiedTime > '2024-01-01T00:00:00'" - Search by name: q="name contains 'report'" - Files in folder: folderId="abc123" or q="'FOLDER_ID' in parents"

name: Find folder

starred.title: Starred
starred.description: Set to true to search for folders that are starred, or false for those that are not.
starred.human_parameter_description: Choose whether to only include folders you've starred (true) or those you haven't (false). Leave blank to ignore this.

page_size.title: Page Size
page_size.description: The maximum number of folders to return in this call (1-1000). This action returns one page per call; use the response's nextPageToken to retrieve additional pages.
page_size.human_parameter_description: How many folders to return in this call. Use the next page token from the response to retrieve more.

name_exact.title: Name Exact
name_exact.description: The exact name of the folder to search for as a string. This search is case-sensitive. Do not pass numbers - convert to string if needed.
name_exact.human_parameter_description: Type the folder's exact name if you know it. This matches the name exactly, including capitalization.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Opaque token for the next page. Omit for the first page, then pass the previous response's nextPageToken unchanged to continue the same search.
page_token.human_parameter_description: Leave blank for the first page. To continue, paste the nextPageToken from the previous response without modifying it.

name_contains.title: Name Contains
name_contains.description: A substring to search for within folder names as a string. This search is case-insensitive.
name_contains.human_parameter_description: Enter a word or phrase that should appear in the folder name. Helpful when you're not sure of the full name.

modified_after.title: Modified After
modified_after.description: Search for folders modified after a specific date and time. The timestamp must be in RFC 3339 format (e.g., '2023-01-15T10:00:00Z' or '2023-01-15T10:00:00.000Z').
modified_after.human_parameter_description: Only show folders updated after this date and time. Use a timestamp like 2023-01-15T10:00:00Z.

parent_folder_id.title: Parent Folder Id
parent_folder_id.description: The ID of the parent folder to search within. Only folders directly inside this parent folder will be returned. You can find parent folder IDs by first searching for the parent folder by name. Supports folders in both My Drive and Shared Drives.
parent_folder_id.human_parameter_description: Search only within a specific parent folder. Paste the ID of the parent folder you want to look inside.

name_not_contains.title: Name Not Contains
name_not_contains.description: A substring to exclude from folder names as a string. Folders with names containing this substring will not be returned. This search is case-insensitive.
name_not_contains.human_parameter_name: Substring to exclude from folder names
name_not_contains.human_parameter_description: Enter a word or phrase that must not appear in the folder name. Use this to filter out folders like 'archive' or 'old'.

full_text_contains.title: Full Text Contains
full_text_contains.description: A string to search for within the folder's name or description (NOT the content of files inside the folder). This search is case-insensitive. Note: Google Drive's fullText search on folders only matches the folder's own metadata, not files contained within.
full_text_contains.human_parameter_description: Enter words that should appear in the folder's name or description. Note: This does NOT search inside files within the folder.

full_text_not_contains.title: Full Text Not Contains
full_text_not_contains.description: A string to exclude from the folder's name or description (NOT the content of files inside the folder). This search is case-insensitive. Note: Google Drive's fullText search on folders only matches the folder's own metadata, not files contained within.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response. Use this for partial responses to request only specific metadata fields. Common fields: id, name, mimeType, webViewLink, webContentLink, createdTime, modifiedTime, size, quotaBytesUsed, parents, owners, permissions. Use '*' to return all available fields. Note: The deprecated v2 field 'alternateLink' is automatically migrated to 'webViewLink'. Example: 'id,name,mimeType,webViewLink,createdTime,modifiedTime'. Most fields (webViewLink, parents, owners, size, modifiedTime, etc.) are omitted by default — explicitly list required fields or use '*' (increases latency). `md5Checksum` is null for native Google Workspace files (Docs/Sheets/Slides); use `mimeType` to classify items — folders use `mimeType='application/vnd.google-apps.folder'` and Workspace files return `size=null`. `modifiedTime` is RFC 3339 UTC format.
